div.head: Had 6
div.ab: And to hadbote, gif fulbrice wyrðe . . ., æt þam V. stæpe V pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
⁊ to hadbote, gif fullbrice wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam fiftan stæpe V pund to bote, mid godcundre scrifte.
⁊ to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurþe, toeacan ðam rihtwere, æt þam fiftan stæpe V pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
Et ad emendationem ordinis (ord. infracturam) in quinto gradu super rectam weram quinque libre (componantur) cum (idonea) penitentia.
And to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere æt þam fiftan stæpe V pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
Und wenn tödtliche Verletzung eintritt: ausser dem gesetzlichen Wergeld beim fünften Ordo als Klerusbusse 5 Pfund zur Busse, neben geistlicher Poenitenz.
And if fatal injury occurs: besides the lawful wergild, for the fifth grade 5 pounds as compensation for orders, with spiritual penance.

And as compensation for one in orders if a full breach of the peace occurs, the perpetrator must make amends for the fifth rank by paying five pounds as a penalty in addition to the standard wergild and by doing spiritual penance.
And in compensation for [an offence against a man in] orders, if a full breach occurs …., one must pay for the fifth degree with five pounds and intercede zealously with ecclesiastical penance.
div.note: D lacks ‘toeacan þam rihtwere’ (Liebermann supplies it).; U: not in Whitelock’s English Historical Documents, which prints only Had 1–2 and 9–11 (with “…” for the rest); the source of this translation is not recorded.
